title: [Feature] Add GLM-5.3-Flash Model Runner V2 support
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds GLM-5.3-Flash Model Runner V2 integration for hybrid cache layout, decode graphs, and MTP. MRV2 must preserve the cache capabilities, shared physical pages, and circular tail addressing contract used by MRV1.

Refs #15665
Refs #16755

- Reuse main's `view_glm5_next_cache()` for kernel-granularity NoPE/indexer views and the packed tail region. Preserve shared MLA/Mamba pages and per-layer bindings.
- Keep copy-on-write layout handling in the existing `models/glm5next/cache_views.py` module, then reuse upstream block copying. Shared MLA/Mamba pages are copied once; separately packed indexer and tail components retain their own strides.
- Reuse upstream `AttentionGroup` directly. SFA/KPool builders restore their layer's logical block size while retaining grouped padding; KPool updates compressed geometry through the existing `set_kernel_block_size()` hook. No factory subclass, concrete-builder dispatch, or `AttentionGroup` symbol replacement remains.
- Carry graph capture lifecycle in KPool metadata, including warmup and rebuilt metadata during multi-step drafting, instead of reading `_EXTRA_CTX.capturing` in the backend.
- Obtain speculative-history requirements from `get_kpool_tail_ring_capacity()` and retain power-of-two ring alignment for the no-prefix coordinator's scheduler-block divisibility contract.
- Generate circular slots in the framework: `request_block[0] * capacity + position % capacity`. This fixes writes to block 0 when compression reads another physical ring. The GLM tail operator and its slot interface remain unchanged.
- Reuse #16755's replicated-tail and empty-component Mooncake handling, and Flash frame sampling for inherited video placeholders.

`AscendBlockTables` owns circular validation and device flags. Only groups with slot mapping enabled participate; disabled groups continue to produce PAD slots. Context parallelism and split physical blocks are rejected only for active circular slot mapping. Ordinary groups retain the `HAS_CIRCULAR=False` specialization. The existing factory and MRV1 proposer are not replaced. Cache views and COW layout handling share the existing model module; this PR does not introduce a layout registry, new capability flags, or a common graph-state enum. No new environment variable or nightly case is introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It enables the tested GLM-5.3-Flash MRV2 graph/MTP path, subject to the source-specific validation below.

SP uses #16804 on a [separate branch](https://github.com/lijiahang226/vllm-ascend/tree/glm53-mrv2-sp-validation). PD end-to-end, Store, CP/PP, other hardware and other quantization formats remain unvalidated. P/D requires compatible tail capacities; Mooncake unit tests do not establish end-to-end PD support.

title: [Performance][Ops] Add FLA NPU backend for GDN prefill
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an opt-in FLA NPU fused backend for Gated Delta Net (GDN) prefill on Ascend A5.

- Adds a dedicated `ascend_gdn_prefill_backend` additional-config key so the Ascend selector does not conflict with vLLM's upstream-injected `gdn_prefill_backend` key.
- Keeps the existing Ascend GDN prefill behavior when the new option is unset: use the built-in CANN fused operator when available and supported, otherwise fall back to the Triton Ascend implementation.
- Accepts only `fla_npu` as an explicit value. 
- Dynamically loads `fla_npu.ops.ascendc.chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` from the external `flash-linear-attention-npu` package only when `fla_npu` is configured. This path targets Ascend A5 and currently requires PCP world size 1.
- Documents the configuration contract and default behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can opt in to the external FLA NPU backend with:

```bash
vllm serve MODEL --additional-config='{"ascend_gdn_prefill_backend":"fla_npu"}'
```

When `ascend_gdn_prefill_backend` is omitted, existing users keep the automatic CANN-to-Triton fallback behavior. If the option is specified, the only valid value is `fla_npu`.

### How was this patch tested?

Added CPU unit-test coverage for:

- the unset default and preservation of the existing backend path;
- loading the external FLA operator through a fake module, without installing or cloning the external repository in standard CI;
- the missing-dependency error path;
- the external operator's extended return tuple and forwarded kernel arguments;
- recurrent-state scattering when empty sequences are filtered from the kernel batch.

CI results for commit `8e2805715`:

- pre-commit: passed;
- mypy: passed;
- CPU unit tests: passed;
- DCO, PR validation, documentation link checks, and Read the Docs builds: passed.

A real A5 end-to-end numerical and performance validation with a compatible `flash-linear-attention-npu` package is still required before merge. The remaining `ci-gate` check requires a maintainer to add one of the repository's ready labels.

title: [BugFix][Attention] Rebuild the sparse MLA plan from the passed indices for MTP drafts
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`sparse_mla` must generate the operator plan from the very tensors the operator
call receives — a plan built over different ones makes the kernel index past what
it was handed. It only regenerated the plan when the query was trimmed to the
unpadded row count, so a replayed FULL graph kept the plan written during
metadata construction.

For the GLM-5.3-Flash MTP draft on A5 (`use_smla=True`) that is fatal: the draft
replays one captured graph per step, and the plan the replayed graph reads can
describe a different step's rows. Its per-row top-k lengths then exceed what each
row's index buffer actually holds and the operator reads the `-1` padding as KV
positions:

```
aicore error, error code = 82
The extend info: errcode:(82) errorStr: The address for MTE2 to write UB and
MTE3 to write L1/UB is out of bounds.
```

Observed on the draft graph replay only: deterministic for one kernel (identical
pc on every run), gone with the draft eager, and absent on A3 (`use_smla=False`,
no plan at all).

This PR rebuilds the plan whenever the draft model is running, deriving the top-k
lengths from the indices actually passed. The target is unchanged: it refreshes
the plan from unpadded host values every step.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests added to `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_nope_metadata.py`:

- `test_a5_smla_rebuilds_plan_for_the_draft_model` — equal-shaped call with the
  draft model running: the plan is regenerated, and the padding row claims zero
  entries even though the prediction said three.
- `test_a5_smla_keeps_the_built_plan_for_the_target` — the equal-shaped target
  call keeps the plan written during metadata construction.

End-to-end on the reporter's A5 deployment (GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8-MXFP8, DP8×TP1+EP,
MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`): before the change the draft
graph replay hit the device error within seconds of the first requests; after the
change the same traffic runs without it.

### Notes

- Relates to #17178, which enables the ACL-graph draft for GLM-Next MTP and is
  what exposes this latent mismatch on A5. 
- The condition is expressed as "the draft model is running" because that is the
  caller whose plan can describe rows it is not passing. A follow-up could derive
  the plan from the indices unconditionally, at the cost of one plan regeneration
  per attention layer per step.
- Still under investigation: the SMLA metadata state is keyed by
  `draft_index=None` on the capture path (`build_for_graph_capture` -> `build` ->
  `_build(draft_index=None)`) but by `draft_index=i` on the runtime path
  (`build_for_drafting`). If that keying is the reason the replayed graph reads a
  stale plan, the capture hook should use the same per-step keying; the change
  here makes the plan correct regardless.

title: [Feature][MRV2] Default Model Runner V2 for all configurations
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR makes Model Runner V2 the default on Ascend when `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is unset. The old architecture, feature, platform, and Triton whitelist is replaced by a blacklist in `vllm_ascend/mrv2_utils.py`.

When the env var is unset, a request uses V2 unless it matches one of these V1 fallbacks:

**Models / platform**

- Hy3-preview (`HYV3*`)
- Gemma4 (`Gemma4*`)
- 310P
- encoder-decoder (Whisper)
- pooling KV

**Features**

- LoRA
- VL encoder disaggregation (`ec_transfer_config` / encoder-only)
- `draft_window_size`
- suffix speculative decoding
- ngram / `ngram_gpu`
- `parallel_drafting`
- dflash2 graph (DFlash2 without `enforce_eager`)

An explicit override still wins:

- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` forces V1
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` forces V2

Upstream GPU / Triton V2 validation does not apply; Ascend owns runner selection.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Unset `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` now defaults to Model Runner V2, except for the blacklist above. Keep V1 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`. Explicit `0` / `1` is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests: `tests/ut/test_mrv2_utils.py` (default V2, blacklist fallback, env override)
- E2E / nightly: default V2 path, plus a few explicit `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` pins
- CI: cpu-ut / e2e on this PR

title: [Feature][Model] Support Kimi K3 PP+DSpark+SP on MRV2
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Compose pipeline parallelism, sequence parallelism and DSpark for Kimi-K3 on Model Runner V2, following the GLM-5.2 DSpark+PP layout (#15747).

K3 with expert parallelism and TP > 1 keeps sequence shards across PP stages (e.g. 8 of 64 rows at TP8), while the V2 receive path slices by the full token count. The fix mirrors MRV1's proven `sync_and_slice_intermediate_tensors` SP branch on the V2 runner: the persistent receive backing is narrowed to a local view around the upstream copy and restored after each invocation. Graph capture is untouched — the sharding lives entirely in the runner's tensor handoff path, like MRV1.

- **Spec+PP support table**: Kimi K3 targets (`KimiLinearForCausalLM`, `KimiK3ForCausalLM`, `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`) join `dspark` support next to DSV4 and GLM-5.2, with aux hidden states and the upstream PP guard bypass. Local K3 MLA (`K3DSparkModel`) and legacy GQA (`Qwen3DSparkModel`) drafts validate as PP=1 on the last stage.
- **PP+SP token sharding** (kimi_k3.py, AttnRes path used by K3 checkpoints): first-stage-only embedding sharding; matching hidden/residual shards carried between stages; last-stage gather; dense MLP layers gather and reduce-scatter around their TP-sharded weights while routed MoE keeps its SP path. Configurations without attention residuals keep the upstream forward unchanged.
- **Aux-state relay**: target stages carry cumulative auxiliary states on the existing transport keys; MLA drafts consume raw prefix sums without the three-dimensional AttnRes bank; legacy GQA keeps materialized capture.
- **Host-position sync**: CPU attention lengths resynchronize on every PP stage after speculative rejection (including stages without a local speculator) and after non-final prefill chunks; attention-metadata preparation waits for the copy.

## Scope notes

- K3 SP+PP under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs is **not** covered by this port (graph capture is untouched) and needs separate validation.
- MRV1 PP+SP support, the tutorial update, e2e and the sandbox-style CPU regression suite from the source branch are excluded per review scope.

## Adaptation since #16511

- `dspark` PP architecture table: union of #16511's K3 entries with main's GLM-5.2 entry.
- The buffer handling nests under main's `pcp_dispatch_context` and keeps the 0.29.0+ `valid_dummy_state_slots` signature.
- The graph-side buffer management from the source branch is dropped; the slicing follows MRV1's naming and placement instead.

### PP draft embedding ownership (follow-up fix)

vLLM main's `maybe_share_target_embed` raises when the K3 DSpark draft loads on the last PP stage — the draft shares the target input embedding (`has_own_embed_tokens = False`, checkpoint copy dropped by the upstream mapper) but the target embedding lives on PP stage 0:

```
RuntimeError: AscendK3DSparkForCausalLM needs the target input embedding, but it is unavailable on this PP stage
```

Following the pattern upstream uses for Qwen3 DSpark (weight-driven `has_own_embed_tokens`), the Ascend draft now constructs a `VocabParallelEmbedding` and loads the frozen `embed_tokens` copy shipped in the draft checkpoint when the real PP group spans multiple stages, and declares `has_own_embed_tokens` on the instance so the share check keeps it instead of raising. `lm_head` still aliases the target's last-stage head. PP=1 keeps upstream aliasing unchanged. Ownership is decided from `get_pp_group().world_size` (the draft's construction config always reports PP=1).

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: Kimi-K3 can run PP+SP and PP+SP+DSpark (eager) on the V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Context-parallel compatibility checks still apply.

## How was this patch tested?

- CPU suites on Ascend aarch64, paired vLLM `84030bbe` — all green (**108 passed**): `tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_pp_sp.py` (basic PP+SP path), `tests/ut/worker/v2/test_pp_utils.py`, `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_pp_mtp.py`, `tests/ut/models/test_kimi_k3_adapter.py`, `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2.py`.
- Functional validation of the underlying implementation: see #16511 (4x8 NPUs, DP1/TP8/PP4, PP+SP+MLA-DSpark, 3x120/120 requests, deterministic correctness probes).
- No hardware rerun for this port, per request.

title: [BugFix][Attention] Fix transdata F.pad row/col swap for non-aligned inputs
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it?**

`transdata` in `vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py` pads a 2-D weight matrix up to a multiple of `block_size` before the NZ (fractal) block reshape. The `F.pad` call passes the row and column pad widths swapped:

```python
nd_mat = F.pad(nd_mat, (0, r_pad, 0, c_pad))
```

PyTorch interprets the 4-tuple from the innermost dimension outward — `(last_dim_left, last_dim_right, dim-2_left, dim-2_right)` — so the code actually pads the **columns** by `r_pad` and the **rows** by `c_pad`, the transpose of the intended `(0, c_pad, 0, r_pad)`.

Consequences for any input not already aligned to the block size:

- The subsequent `reshape((r // b0, b0, c // b1, b1))` receives a tensor of shape `(rows + c_pad, cols + r_pad)` instead of `(r, c)`. When the element count mismatches the call raises `RuntimeError` (e.g. a `(16, 31)` matrix with block `(16, 32)` is padded to `(17, 31)` instead of `(16, 32)`).
- When the element count coincidentally matches, the reshape succeeds but the data is silently misaligned, corrupting the NZ layout.

Both current call sites (`sfa_v1.py:975` `wd_qkv`, `sfa_v1.py:997` `wu_q`) feed dimensions that are multiples of 32, so the padding is a no-op and the bug is latent today; any non-32-aligned weight shape (e.g. new MLAPO model configs) would hit it immediately.

This PR swaps the pad widths to `F.pad(nd_mat, (0, c_pad, 0, r_pad))` and adds CPU unit tests covering a non-aligned input (exact per-block data layout — fails on the old code) and an aligned input (no-op padding).

**Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?**

No. Behavior is unchanged for all currently shipped shapes (where the padding is a no-op); the fix only makes `transdata` correct for non-aligned inputs.

**How was this patch tested?**

- Added regression tests in `tests/ut/attention/test_attention_utils.py`:

### What this PR does / why we need it?

vLLM PR [#52216](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52216) promoted `prefix_cache_retention_interval` from an environment variable to `CacheConfig` / `KVCacheConfig`. title: [Feature][Quant] Introduce combine_quant_mode to force MC2 combine stage communication quantization
body:
### What does this PR do / why we need it?

  Introduces a new top-level Ascend config option `combine_quant_mode` (default `0`, disabled) that lets a model force the MC2 **combine** stage's communication quantization mode regardless of its `quant_type`.

  By default the combine `comm_quant_mode` passed to`torch.moe_distribute_combine_v2` is derived from the model's quant type (e.g. `W8A8MXFP` → `4`). When a user sets `combine_quant_mode` to a non-zero value, the combine comm quant mode is forced to that value instead, so non-MXFP models can opt into a specific combine communication quant mode (e.g. `4` = MXFP communication quantization) without changing the model weights' quantization.

  Precedence in `get_combine_mc_kwargs`:
  1. explicit `comm_quant_mode` set by a deeper per-layer quant config still wins, so the switch never silently overrides a deliberate quant decision;
  2. `additional_config.combine_quant_mode` when non-zero;
  3. otherwise the existing `quant_type`-based default.

  ### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

  Yes — a new optional `additional_config` key `combine_quant_mode` (int). It is documented in the additional-configuration table. Default behavior is unchanged (`0` = use the model's own quant).

  ### How was this patch tested?

  - New unit tests:
    - `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`: default is `0`, int-string `"4"` is lax-coerced to `4`, non-integer values are rejected.
    - `tests/ut/ops/a2/test_token_dispatcher.py`: non-zero `combine_quant_mode` forces the combine comm quant mode for a non-MXFP model; `0` keeps the default; an explicit `comm_quant_mode` still takes precedence.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

  Part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/13318

  - **`enable_sparse_*_c8` gating is tied to the actual quantized dtype**, so the C8 sparse enter/exit layouts only activate when the dtype is fp8/int8.
  - **Two new patches** make this work on vLLM builds that lack the pluggable kv-cache-dtype mechanism (e.g. `releases/v0.27.1`):
    - `worker/patch_kv_cache_dtype.py`: flips `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE["fp8"]`  to `torch.float8_e4m3fn` in every worker when `register_kv_cache_dtype` is unavailable (no-op on `kvquant_27`+).

title: [BugFix] Pad negative positions in every group of the fused slot mapping
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17528.

`positions` is shared by every KV-cache group of a fused slot-mapping
launch, but since #16537 the fused kernels pad negative positions only in
circular groups. In a mixed circular/non-circular layout (DSV4.1's
compressor state, GLM-5-Next's indexer tail) a non-circular group turns a
negative position into a real-looking slot ID. For `pos <= -block_size`
the block-table window base goes negative and the load leaves the
request's row. It is latent today (MRV1 positions are non-negative); the
standalone repro in #17528 shows the wrong slot IDs on 910B2.

Changes:

- Under `HAS_CIRCULAR`, negative positions are excluded from the window
  base, the base is clamped into the row, and they map to `PAD_ID` in
  every group.
- `MultiGroupBlockTable` passes `is_circular_ptr=None` when no group is
  circular (today it always passes the tensor), so engines without a
  circular group, e.g. plain DSV4, compile the path out.

The same change is part of #17529 (runtime recompile fix, #17527).
Whichever lands first, the other rebases trivially.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Negative positions in mixed layouts now map to `PAD_SLOT_ID` in every
group; no current caller produces them.

### How was this patch tested?

New `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_compute_slot_mapping_fused_negative_positions.py`:
negative positions across the adaptive small/large-tile and parallel
kernels (sharing a tile with regular tokens, `pos <= -block_size`, a whole
negative request) in a mixed layout and an all-circular control, plus
`is_circular_ptr=None` equivalence. On 910B2: 16 passed. The fused-kernel
portion of `test_glm5next_tail_slot_mapping_triton.py` (mixed circular layout
across three length shapes, NPU-graph capture/replay, and the no-descriptor
single-group call) passes bit-identically with and without this patch; the
nightly test itself is broken on main since #16925 (its `BlockTable.__new__`
harness predates the DSV4.1 block-table rewrite: missing `is_circular_group`,
numpy-style draft harness, drifted single-group expectations) and fails 4/4

of being claimed as a gate. The standalone repro from #17528 goes from

title: [BugFix][Performance] Bound fused slot-mapping JIT specializations and prewarm them
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17527.

The fused multi-group slot-mapping kernels from #15289 take `NUM_REQS` and
`PARALLEL_TILES` as `tl.constexpr`. Every new `(num_reqs, tile)` pair seen at
runtime therefore compiles a new Triton specialization on the hot path
(~5.5 s bisheng compile on 910B2), and every in-flight request stalls for
the whole compile. On DSV4-Flash + MRV1 at concurrency 64 this cost ~1.8x
throughput on average over 5 rounds (413 vs 762 tok/s). Details and
evidence are in #17527.

Changes:

1. `num_reqs` / `parallel_tiles` become `do_not_specialize` runtime
   arguments, and the kernels launch on a `(group, req[, tile])` grid.
   `_select_slot_mapping_launch_config` is unchanged, so every shape picks
   the same kernel and tile as before. The key space becomes 7 per
   `HAS_CIRCULAR` variant: adaptive tiles 16..512 plus the parallel
   `TILE_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`. The values are not recovered from
   `tl.num_programs()`: on 910B2 that form added ~27 us device time per
   call (msprof `aiv_time`).
2. A new `slot_mapping` entry in `kernel_warmup` prewarms all of those
   keys. It runs after `initialize_kv_cache`, when the multi-group block
   table exists, and before graph capture. `profile_run` is too early: the
   input batch still has one block table there, so the fused path isn't
   set up.
3. `MultiGroupBlockTable` passes `is_circular_ptr=None` when no group is
   circular, so the circular path is compiled out (today every engine runs
   it), and the hot-loop `int32 % block_size` becomes a multiply-subtract.
   For engines without a circular group (e.g. DSV4) the kernel's device
   time drops to 0.10x-0.76x of main.
4. Under `HAS_CIRCULAR`, negative positions are padded in every group and
   kept out of the block-table window base (#17528, latent). This part
   is also available standalone as #17530. With it, engines that do have a
   circular group (DSV4.1, GLM-5-Next) take 1.05x-1.61x of main's device
   time (+1 to +7 us per call); it can be dropped from this PR if preferred.

Relation to open PRs: #16829 marks `NUM_REQS` `do_not_specialize`, which is
change 1 without `PARALLEL_TILES`. It has no prewarm, so each key still
compiles once on the hot path after a cold start. #17353 (draft) uses
`tl.num_programs(1)`, see the note in change 1. This PR is a superset of
#16829; happy to rebase onto it if it lands first.

Backport: #15530 already brought the fused kernel to `releases/v0.26.0rc`
(not in any tag yet), so this fix should go there too before the next
release from that branch; happy to open the cherry-pick.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. Engine startup gains the slot-mapping
prewarm. On an empty Triton cache that is a one-time ~40 s per worker
(7 keys x ~5.5 s, before graph capture); with a warm cache the keys load
from disk. Negative positions in mixed circular/non-circular layouts now
map to `PAD_SLOT_ID` in every group (no current caller produces them).

### How was this patch tested?

On 8x 910B2, CANN 9.1.0, vLLM 0.30.0, at base `39fef3f8f`:

- `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_compute_slot_mapping_fused_groups.py`
  (new): 29 passed. It covers the #15289 shape matrix against the
  per-group kernel, negative positions (including `pos <= -block_size`
  and all-negative requests), `is_circular_ptr=None` equivalence, bounded

  directly and through `MultiGroupBlockTable`.
- `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/`: 21 passed, including the new
  `test_slot_mapping_triton_warmup.py`.

  200 prompts at concurrency 64:
  - main: 4 of 5 rounds stalled at 262-373 tok/s with 6.3-6.5 s stalls;
    the clean round did 762 tok/s.
  - this PR's kernel, warm Triton cache: 6 of 6 rounds clean, 749-763
    tok/s, zero ITL > 1 s, no new slot-mapping cache entries.
  - this PR, empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`: `slot_mapping Triton warmup

title: [Feature][Kernel] Extend split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope with value normalization for Gemma4
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Gemma4 runs its pre-attention chain (qkv split, per-head q/k RMSNorm, RoPE, and a weight-less per-head **v** RMSNorm) as separate ops on Ascend. The existing fused `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` kernel cannot cover it because it copies V straight out of the fused QKV tensor, and the existing `qknorm_rope_fusion_pass` has no notion of the V norm. This PR adds a `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope_vnorm` Triton kernel and a graph fusion pattern that rewrites Gemma4's pre-attention chain into it. It replaces the `Gemma4Attention` monkey-patch used in the earlier revision of this PR, as requested in review. **Kernel.** A variant of `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` that normalizes V instead of copying it. Because V now needs the same float32 reduction scratch as Q and K, the separate wide-tile V loop that the base kernel uses for the plain copy no longer pays for itself, so V is folded into the q/k loop: - one `tl.load` covers the whole fused row (`total_hidden_size`) instead of two separate column segments; - one RMSNorm reduction covers every q, k **and** v head of the tile, reshaped to `(tile * (q_head_num + 2*kv_head_num), HEAD_DIM)`; - Q, K and V are then cut out with three `extract_slice` calls at head offsets `0`, `q_head_num` and `q_head_num + kv_head_num`. Q and K apply their weights and RoPE; V has neither, so it is a cast and a store that reuses the K output index and mask. This is valid because Gemma4's `v_norm` is the same per-head RMSNorm with the same `eps` and no learnable scale; only the weight application moves after the shared reduction. The kernel keeps everything else from `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope`: the 1-D grid over vector cores, the batched UB tiling, the per-tile cos/sin gather shared by all heads, and partial-RoPE support. The UB tiling factor grows by `4 * kv_hidden_size` to account for the V columns now living in the tile. **Fusion pass.** `QKVNormRopeFusionPattern` in `qknorm_rope_fusion_pass.py` matches the unfused chain (qkv split, per-head `npu_rms_norm` on q and k, `npu_rotary_embedding`, per-head `npu_rms_norm` on v) and replaces it with the new kernel. - **One pattern per attention shape.** Gemma4 alternates sliding layers (`head_dim` 256) and full attention layers (`head_dim` 512, fewer KV heads), and `register_replacement` bakes the split sizes and head counts into the traced pattern. The pass therefore registers the pattern once per distinct `(head_dim, num_heads, num_kv_heads)` among the model's attention layers, the same approach as vLLM's own `qk_norm_rope_fusion` pass. - **Dedup key.** `BasePattern` gains a `pattern_key()` method, which this pattern extends with its shape. Without it, the second shape's registration would be silently skipped. Existing patterns keep their keys unchanged. - **Rejecting other shapes.** The matcher treats split sizes as wildcards and rejects a graph of another shape by re-tracing the pattern against it. A size mismatch makes `split` raise `ValueError`, which the pattern converts to the `RuntimeError` the matcher treats as "no match", as vLLM's `qk_norm_rope_fusion` does. - The existing q/k-only patterns are unchanged and keep their `head_dim == 128` guard, so they cannot claim the q/k half of a Gemma4 layer and leave its v norm unfused. - The replacement applies no v weight. Every `v_norm` in upstream vLLM today is weight-less; a model with a learnable v norm would need the kernel extended first. **Proportional RoPE.** Full attention layers use `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding`, which implements proportional RoPE by zero-padding `inv_freq` and passing `rotary_dim=head_size` to the base class. Its cos/sin cache is therefore an ordinary full-width cache whose non-rotated pairs hold cos=1 and sin=0, and the kernel needs no layer-type knowledge. Upstream `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding` had no Ascend override, so these layers ran the PyTorch `rotate_half` implementation, which the pattern cannot match. This PR registers `AscendGemma4RotaryEmbedding`, which keeps Gemma4's cos/sin cache and runs the NPU rotary kernel (`npu_rotary_embedding`), as sliding layers already do. **When a layer fuses.** The pattern is registered when: - the model dtype is bfloat16 and Triton is available; - the hardware profile supports the new `HardwareCapability.GRAPH_QKV_NORM_ROPE_FUSION` (Atlas A2/A3). Ascend 950 routes `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` to a SIMT kernel and has no SIMT variant of this operator yet, so it keeps the unfused chain; - one token's tile fits a vector core's unified buffer. For gemma-4-31B, full attention layers need tensor parallel size 4 or more; below that they stay unfused and the pass logs it once. Layers that cannot match stay unfused without any check: KV-shared layers have no k/v norm, and a norm bias is applied as a separate add. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No API change. In graph mode (the default), Gemma4 on Atlas A2/A3 uses the fused pre-attention path automatically. The existing `fuse_qknorm_rope` option in `ascend_compilation_config` turns it off, together with the existing q/k fusion. With `enforce_eager`, no fusion pass runs and Gemma4 keeps the unfused chain. Full attention layers now run RoPE on the NPU rotary kernel instead of the PyTorch implementation, including when they stay unfused. ### How was this patch tested? Tested on 910B1, TP=4, dtype bfloat16 with gemma4-31b-it. **Performance** **Accuracy** | Benchmark | Unfused (baseline) | Fused (this PR) | |-----------|-------------------:|----------------:| | HumanEval | 96.74 | 96.74 | | GPQA | 76.09 | 76.28 | Averaged over 3 runs. **Correctness** pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

title: [Feature][EPLB] Integrate STAIR policy with Model Runner V2
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

This is PR 6/6 of the STAIR EPLB series proposed in #17506. It integrates the preceding data-plane, statistics, transfer, and planning components into Model Runner V2 without changing the legacy V1 policy path.

Common baseline: `9f1af00c7fcd7c22cf0c791ab9f6c8d98402ec06` (`upstream/main` on 2026-09-24).

Dependencies:

- #17508 — MRV2 routing and load-recording data plane
- #17509 — policy-prepared temporal load statistics
- #17510 — explicit-source asynchronous transfer
- #17511 — STAIR load and replica planner
- #17512 — constrained STAIR placement

The visible diff is cumulative while those dependencies are open. Review this PR after, or on top of, the five dependency PRs.

The integration:

- selects `default` or `stair` exclusively through the upstream `EPLBConfig.policy` field;
- keeps MRV2 `additional_config.eplb_config` limited to `load_collection_phase` and detailed `stair_config` tuning;
- constructs policies through a small factory and keeps the default policy on the upstream behavior;
- uses the existing EPLB CPU group to statically shard PP-stage-local layers and reconstruct the deterministic plan with all-gather, without a rank-0 planning coordinator;
- preserves weighted temporal bins through the common `rebalance_experts` entry point;
- runs STAIR's CPU planning in one persistent child process with bounded BLAS threads and a framed NPZ/JSON local protocol (`allow_pickle=False`);
- supplies stage-local node topology and per-layer ratios from the last placement that actually committed;
- attaches exact source coordinates for constrained asynchronous transfers and advances hysteresis anchors only after the corresponding layer commits;
- logs committed-cycle mean/p95 ratios before and after planning, changed-layer count, cross-rank transfer count, and cross-node transfer count.

The architecture intentionally keeps generic EPLB lifecycle and publication in `AscendEplbState`, policy-specific statistics and planning in `StairEplbPolicy`, and narrow upstream compatibility adapters in `patch_eplb.py`. This allows future policies to reuse the framework without inheriting STAIR's binning, covariance, subprocess, or placement constraints.

RFC: #17506

Upstream extensibility context: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33549

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Model Runner V2 can select the STAIR EPLB policy and tune its advanced parameters. Defaults are intended to work without tuning. The upstream `default` policy remains selectable for experiments and compatibility.

## How was this patch tested?

- 263 focused CPU unit tests passed across STAIR planning, process protocol, layer sharding, policy statistics, explicit transfer, state, platform adapters, MRV2 controller, load collection, and configuration.
- Two source-tree-only checks were excluded locally: construction of a real NPU event on a CPU-only host, and a subprocess import check that requires the generated package `_build_info` module.
- `bash format.sh ci` passed, including Ruff, spelling, markdown, secret scan, forbidden-import, and repository-specific checks.
- Real NPU multi-node validation and CI are intentionally pending while this draft stack is reviewed and rebased independently.

title: [Ops][Feature] Enable A5 MegaMoe for pure prefill
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Port #16048 and its CI fixes to `main`, retaining the CANN MegaMoe integration from #15519, including the CANN 9.2 communication-context module path and pure-prefill selection validated on Ascend 950DT.

With `enable_fused_mc2=2`, supported A5 W4A8 MXFP layers with DP=1 use MegaMoe for pure prefill even when the batch exceeds the decode MC2 token capacity. Decode and mixed batches retain the existing communication selection. Layer capabilities determine whether the quantization, activation, shape and EP layout are supported; the runtime passes the MXFP weight/scale layouts and SiTU parameters to the CANN operator.

The runtime gate is checked by the selector, operator initialization and DP synchronization policy. `0` disables fused MC2; `1` retains the legacy path without enabling CANN MegaMoe; `2` opts into CANN MegaMoe. Disabled runs skip CANN capability probing and binding preload. A5 validates the instantiated layer rather than the legacy checkpoint quantization filter.

The port preserves the target branch's existing non-A5 receive-buffer policy. A5 passes additional_config.mega_moe_max_tokens directly as max_recv_token_num (default 65536); 131072 can be configured for a larger receive capacity. CANN's native loader handles bindings; this change adds no C++ or device-kernel implementation.

MRV2 now passes the target model and pure-prefill metadata to the same selector. The model context is scoped to target execution and restored on success or failure; dummy/profile calls do not expose target capabilities. The platform hook also supplies the existing MegaMoe and decode-node context fields.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Supported A5 W4A8 MXFP prefill can enable MegaMoe with:

```bash
vllm serve <model> \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --additional-config '{"enable_fused_mc2": 2, "mega_moe_max_tokens": 131072}'
```

The validated CANN 9.2 package provides `cann_ops_transformer.ops.mc2.common.comm_context`. Missing native binding caches may be built by the CANN loader on first use. Warm up the intended prefill shapes before profiling.

title: [CI] Improve nightly image build and publishing workflow
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
The manually triggered nightly image build workflow previously supported building a specific vLLM commit together with a specific vLLM Ascend commit. However, it had several limitations:

1. `vllm_commit` only accepted a commit hash and could not directly use a vLLM release tag such as `v0.29.0`.
2. Temporary image names truncated the vLLM revision to seven characters. This is appropriate for commit hashes, but truncates release tags and may cause ambiguous image names.
3. The A5 Dockerfiles always cloned vLLM by tag and did not explicitly support checking out an exact vLLM commit.
4. Images built from specified commits were limited to the temporary repository, making it difficult to reuse them as the base image for subsequent `nightly-ci-*` builds.
5. The separate `tag` and `branch` workflow inputs consumed two manual-dispatch input slots and made it difficult to add an explicit publishing option.

This PR updates the nightly image build workflow so that a complete pipeline can be run with specified vLLM and vLLM Ascend revisions:

1. Build the base image from the specified revisions.
2. Optionally publish a daily build using the release-compatible `nightly-main[-suffix]` tags.
3. Reuse that image when building `nightly-ci-main-a2`, `nightly-ci-main-a3`, and other nightly CI images.
4. Run nightly tests against the same vLLM Ascend revision contained in the selected base image.

#### Support vLLM release tags in commit mode

The `vllm_commit` workflow input now accepts either:

- A 7–40 character hexadecimal commit hash.
- A vLLM release tag such as `v0.29.0`, `v0.30.0rc1`, or a supported post/dev release tag.

The image build passes only one corresponding Docker build argument:

- `VLLM_COMMIT` when a commit hash is provided.
- `VLLM_TAG` when a release tag is provided.

This allows release builds to preserve the correct vLLM version metadata, which is required by version-dependent code paths such as `vllm_version_is()`.

The `vllm_ascend_commit` input remains an exact commit hash so that the selected vLLM Ascend source revision is deterministic.

#### Support exact vLLM commits in A5 Dockerfiles

`Dockerfile.a5` and `Dockerfile.a5.openEuler` now accept an optional `VLLM_COMMIT` build argument.

When `VLLM_COMMIT` is provided, the Dockerfile initializes the vLLM repository, fetches the specified commit, and checks out `FETCH_HEAD`. Otherwise, it keeps the existing tag-based shallow clone behavior using `VLLM_TAG`.

This keeps the default A5 build behavior unchanged while ensuring that commit-mode builds actually use the requested vLLM commit.

#### Preserve complete vLLM release tags in temporary image names

For commit hashes, temporary image names continue to use the first seven characters.

For release tags, the complete tag is retained. For example:

```text
vllm_commit=v0.29.0
vllm_ascend_commit=abcdef123456...

vllm-ascend-v0.29.0-abcdef1
```

This prevents release tags from being truncated and avoids collisions between versions that share the same initial characters.

#### Combine Docker branch and tag inputs

The separate `tag` and `branch` workflow inputs are replaced by a single `docker_ref` choice input.

The values are interpreted as follows:

- `main` and `releases/*` select a branch.
- `v*` selects a release tag.
- `tag:main` preserves the previous manual Docker tag behavior for `main`.
- `none` enables commit mode when both revision inputs are provided.

This preserves the existing branch and tag build paths while freeing a workflow-dispatch input slot for the publishing option.

External scripts that manually dispatch the workflow must replace the old `tag` or `branch` parameter with `docker_ref`.

#### Publish specified revisions for downstream nightly CI builds

Commit-mode builds now follow these publishing rules:

| Build type | `publish_nightly_main` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `release` | `false` or `true` | Publish using `nightly-main[-suffix]` |
| `daily` | `false` | Keep the existing temporary-only behavior |
| `daily` | `true` | Publish using the release-compatible `nightly-main[-suffix]` tags |

The publishing switch only changes daily commit-mode behavior. Release commit builds already publish their final image and therefore do not depend on this option.

When `publish_nightly_main` is enabled for a daily commit build:

- The image is still built with the selected daily dependencies and CANN image.
- The final multi-architecture image is published to the same repository used by release nightly images.
- The final image uses the same `nightly-main[-suffix]` naming convention as a release build.
- The dated daily tag is not used as the final published tag for this promotion path.

For example:

```text
nightly-main
nightly-main-a3
nightly-main-310p
nightly-main-a5
nightly-main-openeuler
nightly-main-a3-openeuler
```

This is required because release-mode nightly CI image builds use images such as:

```text
swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main
```

as their base image. Publishing a daily build only with a CANN-versioned and dated tag would not be picked up by the subsequent `nightly-ci-*` workflow.

After promotion, manually triggering a nightly CI build with `build_type=release` produces images such as:

```text
nightly-ci-main-a2
nightly-ci-main-a3
nightly-ci-main-310p
nightly-ci-main-a5
```

These images inherit the exact vLLM and vLLM Ascend revisions already contained in the promoted `nightly-main` base image. The downstream Docker build does not replace them with the latest vLLM Ascend `main` source.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The manual workflow dispatch interface changes in the following ways:

- The previous `tag` and `branch` inputs are replaced by `docker_ref`.
- `vllm_commit` accepts either a commit hash or a vLLM release tag.
- A new `publish_nightly_main` checkbox is available for daily commit-mode builds.
- Release commit-mode builds publish `nightly-main[-suffix]` images directly.
- Daily commit-mode builds can explicitly promote their output to the same release-compatible image names.

The publishing option defaults to `false`, so daily commit builds retain their temporary-only behavior unless promotion is explicitly requested.

Scheduled builds, pull request label builds, and existing daily builds that do not enable this option retain their previous publishing behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

title: [v0.26.0rc][Ops][BugFix] Register padded hybrid KV cache spans
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is the `releases/v0.26.0rc` adaptation of #16129.

The v0.26 connector normally registers `kv_cache_tensor.size`, which remains the lower bound in this patch. For 0.26-derived deployments that expose padded runtime KV tensor views, however, the physical span addressed by block-stride transfers can exceed that configured logical size.

The connector now records each runtime tensor's end as:

```text
data_ptr + shape[0] * stride(0) * element_size
```

and registers the larger of:

- the existing `kv_cache_tensor.size`; and
- the runtime span from the lowest tensor address to the highest tensor end.

This preserves the native v0.26 layout while preventing high block IDs from falling outside Mooncake's registered region when a hybrid KV tensor includes inter-block padding.

The observed DeepSeek V4 indexer layout had a 4096-byte payload and a 4160-byte block stride. Registering only the logical payload caused a high-block remote-buffer lookup failure, followed by HCCL/AICPU and sampling failures.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. Hybrid P/D KV transfer registration now covers padded runtime tensor layouts.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added unit coverage for a padded `as_strided` tensor.
- Added connector-level coverage verifying that a configured 12-byte region is expanded to its 18-byte runtime stride span.
- `python -m py_compile vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_hybrid_connector.py tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_hybrid_connector.py`
- `git diff --check`
- The root cause and stride-span correction were validated on an Ascend A3 DeepSeek V4 P/D + DSpark deployment based on the v0.26 nightly image; the same high-block transfer succeeded and pressure testing completed more than 30,000 audited transfers without OOB, transfer failure, NaN, IndexCheck, or EZ9999.

The focused pytest target could not start in the Windows checkout because the matching vLLM test dependency set is incomplete (`cbor2` is missing); CI is expected to run the added tests.

title: [Feature] Add online MXFP8 quantization support for float checkpoints on Ascend A5
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds online W8A8 MXFP8 quantization support for Ascend A5.

Currently, the `ascend` quantization method mainly relies on offline quantized checkpoints generated by ModelSlim. This requires users to prepare MXFP8 checkpoints before deployment, which increases the deployment complexity.

This change enables users to load original BF16/FP16 checkpoints and quantize weights to MXFP8 during model loading. The implementation reuses the existing `AscendModelSlimConfig` and vLLM's `quantization_config_dict_json` override mechanism without introducing a new quantization entry point.

Example:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --quantization ascend \
    --hf-overrides '{
        "quantization_config_dict_json": {
            "online_quantization": true,
            "model_quant_type": "W8A8_MXFP8",
            "group_size": 32,
            "ignore": ["lm_head"]
        }
    }'

title: [Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
body:
[Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR introduces `ECMemcacheConnector`, a MemCache-backed L1 cache
for multimodal encoder outputs. It integrates with vLLM through the
existing EC connector framework and uses the multimodal feature
identifier (`mm_hash`) as the cache key.

Repeated image or video inputs can reuse previously computed encoder
embeddings instead of running the multimodal encoder again.

- Add a scheduler-side MemCache client that checks multiple `mm_hash`
  values in one request and records cache hits and misses.
- Send per-step load/save metadata from the scheduler to workers:
  cache hits are loaded from MemCache, while misses run the encoder and
  publish the resulting embeddings.
- Load multiple encoder outputs directly into preallocated NPU tensors
  with `batch_get_into`.
- Use `KeyInfo.size()` together with the model dtype and encoder hidden
  dimension to reconstruct each cached tensor as
  `[num_encoder_tokens, hidden_dim]`.
- Publish newly computed encoder outputs directly from NPU memory with
  `put_from`.
- Record an NPU event before dispatching the put operation to a background
  thread, so MemCache waits for encoder computation without blocking the
  model-runner thread.
- Save only from TP rank 0 and PCP rank 0. Encoder outputs are identical
  across TP/PCP ranks, so publishing from every rank would duplicate data
  and cause concurrent writes to the same `mm_hash`.
- Keep eviction management inside MemCache. The connector does not add a
  separate local eviction policy.
- Track cumulative cache hits, misses, and hit rate for debugging and
  observability.

This PR also extends MemcacheBackend with:
- batch_get_into, for copying multiple values into flat destination
  buffers.
- put_from, for publishing one value directly from a device buffer.
- Optional transfer-direction arguments for the existing get and put
  wrappers while preserving their previous default directions.
When the connector is not configured, the existing encoder execution and
cache behavior remain unchanged.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
Yes, when ECMemcacheConnector is explicitly enabled.

The connector can be enabled without modifying vLLM:

```bash
vllm serve <model> \
  --ec-transfer-config '{
     "ec_connector": "ECMemcacheConnector",
     "ec_connector_module_path": "vllm_ascend.distributed.ec_transfer.ec_memcache_connector",
     "ec_role": "ec_both",

}'

title: [BugFix][KVTransfer] Keep AscendStore receive registration until completion
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #16460.

When a request is aborted while waiting for an asynchronous AscendStore load, the core scheduler retains its KV blocks until receive completion. AscendStore currently removes the request from `_loading_req_ids` when it sees `finished_req_ids`. The worker filters receive completions against that set, so the completion is never reported and the deferred release cannot finish.

Keep the receive registration across request termination, and clear it through the existing `update_finished_recving()` method when connector output reports completion. This also clears registrations after normal receives. The scheduler's ownership assertions, worker completion filter and preemption cleanup remain unchanged.

Updated against upstream `bea70ab8` on September 25 as a single linear commit. This replaces the previous merge-based update, whose original commit conflicted when CI replayed it with `git rebase`. The file tree is unchanged from `51674873`, and a local replay of the CI rebase command passed. The send-side cleanup from #16119 is preserved; the send-state regression checks the current `sending_events` and `sending_blocks` bookkeeping. This PR still changes only the scheduler and its unit tests.

Related work: #14132 addresses load/save co-queueing. #16119 removes the synchronous-save delayed-free handshake but leaves this receive-registration path unchanged. This change addresses missing receive completion, distinct from the late notification for an already-removed request described in vllm-project/vllm#43226.

title: [Feature][Model] Enable DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on Ascend950 (A5)
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enables **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on Ascend950 (A5)**.

Before this change the model starts but is unusable: generation is garbled and loops, and DSpark accepts only the first speculative position.

#### Root cause of the garbled output

The A5 `HcPre` kernel ignores the `pre_mix` weights it is given and collapses the four hyper-connection streams by its own internally computed coefficients. At layer 0 all four streams are the token embedding, so the layer input becomes

```
y = (sum of the kernel's own coefficients) x embedding = 0.356 x embedding
```

instead of `1.0 x embedding`. Every layer is fed its input scaled down by ~2.8x, and the error compounds through the stack. The same kernel also leaves its optional mixing-coefficient output unwritten.

`DeepseekV41DecoderLayer.hc_pre` now performs both reductions itself. The combination is the same weighted sum `hc_collapse` already implements, so no numerical behaviour is invented:

```python
y = (pre_mix.unsqueeze(-1) * x.float()).sum(-2).to(x.dtype)
```

DSpark is fixed by the same change: the draft model consumes the main model's hidden states, so once those were wrong the draft could not match beyond the first position.

#### The rest of the A5 enablement

| Area | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Attention | Use `SparseFlashMla` on A5 instead of `npu_sparse_attn_sharedkv`, with `PA_BBND` layout and sliding-window `ori` masking |
| CSA odd-length trap | Duplicate one query per request so no request ever presents an odd packed query count (AI core 507015) |
| Compressed KV geometry | Derive the storage block size from `tokens_per_state`; a compress-ratio-2 plane stores half a logical block per page |
| MoE dispatch | Fall back to AllGather on A5, where `aclnnMoeDistributeDispatchV4` fails with 561000 (gated on `DSV4_COMPRESSED_CACHE`, other SoCs unaffected) |
| Quantization | Select the FP8 scheme from the checkpoint's `weight_block_size`; released V4.1-Flash ships 32-wide blocks and must skip the 128x128 to 32x1 scale reorganization |
| Indexer | Select TopK straight from the compressed stream: `quant_lightning_indexer_v2` only implements the two-level candidate path in its arch22 kernel |
| Plan construction | Resolve `npu_sparse_attn_sharedkv` at call time, since V4.1 builds the DSA plan while configuring the KV cache |
| Custom ops | Add `sparse_flash_mla`, `sparse_flash_mla_metadata` and `rms_norm_cast` to the ascend950 build list |

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new flags or configuration. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash simply works on A5.

### How was this patch tested?

Hardware: Ascend950PR, 8 cards, TP8 + EP, released `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` weights.

```bash
vllm serve /data/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --served-model-name dsv41 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 --max-model-len 1000000 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 10 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":64}' \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code \
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy \
  --quantization deepseek_v4_fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enforce_eager":true}'
```

**Generation quality.** A 1M-token context serves with the KV pool clamped to 9,592,505 tokens (9.59x concurrency for 1M-token requests). An 800-word Chinese essay prompt finishes on its own at 1247 tokens, 50.9 tok/s, with every date and name correct. Mixed long/short/long requests answer correctly and hit the prefix cache (0.2s on the repeated 532-token prompt).

**Dataset accuracy (GSM8K).** 5-shot GSM8K over `/v1/chat/completions`, `temperature=0`, thinking disabled, answer taken as the last number in the reply, scored against the `####` gold value:

| Setting | Samples | exact_match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5-shot | 200 | **190 / 200 = 95.0%** |
| 5-shot | 50 | 50 / 50 = 100% |

One of the ten misses is a formatting difference only (`57.00` against a gold of `57`). Two replies out of 200 hit the 512-token cap; the mean reply is 121 tokens, so generation terminates on its own.

This was measured on the command above with `--max-model-len 69632` and `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.


**Concurrent serving.** SparseFlashMla does not keep requests independent when several are packed into one TND batch: only the request at row 0 is computed from its own rows. A batch of identical requests is unaffected, so this stayed hidden until concurrent requests carried different content. Attention now issues one call per request. With 16 requests in flight at once (6 five-shot GSM8K, 6 short factual questions, 4 open-ended 150-word answers):

| Workload | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 5-shot GSM8K | 5 / 6 correct, every reply ended on its own |
| Short factual questions | 6 / 6 correct, 2 - 3 tokens each |
| Open-ended answers | 4 / 4 coherent, all ended on their own |

Before the fix the same 8-way GSM8K load scored 3/40 with 32 of the 40 replies running to the token cap, and open-ended answers degenerated into a repeated token.

**Agreement with a known-good reference.** Compared against a working DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash deployment on the same weights:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layers with identical routed-expert sets | 3/40 | 30/40 |
| Mean expert overlap | 3.0/6 | 5.72/6 |
| DSpark per-position acceptance | 0.135, 0, 0, 0, 0 | 0.61, 0.35, 0.17, 0.09, 0.05 |
| Mean acceptance length | ~1.1 | 1.8 - 2.3 |

Short-prompt logit distributions now match the reference to within bf16 noise, including top-5 ordering.

**Unit tests.** `tests/ut` was run against this branch and against unmodified main in the same container to separate pre-existing failures (missing `acl` module and LoRA ops in that image) from real regressions. Test updates in this PR cover the A5 behaviour changes: the `hc_pre` contract, A5 MoE dispatch collapsing to AllGather, and metadata fixtures gaining `num_reqs`.

title: [Feat][Quantization] Support W4A8 dynamic linear layers
fix(attention): maintain per-query causal KV boundaries in FIA for DFlash
body:
## Problem

When multiple queries are folded into a single `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (FIA) call — which happens in DFlash speculative decoding verify, and in grouped prefill — query groups can incorrectly share a causal KV length. Queries that should see different KV extents end up in the same group, producing wrong attention outputs (token-level diff vs eager reference).

Additionally, the CANN FAI kernel processes KV in `MAX_KV_STACK_LEN=512` chunks and uses special reduction trees when the tail block has exactly 256 or 512 columns. Rows ending at those positions must be isolated into separate groups to keep bf16 online-softmax reduction order deterministic across different query groupings.

## Root cause

In `vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py`, when constructing FIA metadata for multi-query batches:

1. **Causal boundary violation**: queries with different causal KV visibility were grouped together in a single FIA call, so earlier queries could see KV belonging to later queries
2. **Reduction order instability**: query groups crossing 256/512-column tail boundaries changed the online-softmax reduction path (`CalcLocalRowSum` special tree vs `RowsumTAILTILE`), producing bf16 drift

## Fix

This PR adds per-query causal metadata expansion before the FIA call:

- `kv_boundary_metadata.py`: plans query groups that respect both causal boundaries and the 256/512 special reduction positions. Short queries (≤16) and long prefill queries (≤128) are grouped, but never across a causal boundary or a special reduction position
- `query_invariant.py`: `expand_query_metadata()` builds the expanded read-only metadata; `query_invariant_attention()` calls FIA with per-group `actual_seq_lengths` and `actual_seq_lengths_kv`
- `graph_query_metadata.py`: graph-capture-safe metadata builder (strongly-owned table, refreshed per step)
- `attention_v1.py`: hooks the fix into the eager forward path

Key properties:
- **Read-only**: metadata is reused across layers, never used for cache writes
- **No KV ownership change**: block tables, slot mappings, prefix cache behavior all unchanged
- **Coverage**: applies to all causal target queries (verify, prefill, chunked prefill), not just short verify blocks

## Reproduction evidence

- 155-request full corpus, cold+hot, target+dflash: 620 complete EOS responses, all token-exact with eager reference
- DFlash QPM improved from 43.5 (corrected naive per-query) to 76.4 (boundary grouping)
- NPU matrix tests: 160 boundary cases all bit-exact, including 256/512 tail positions, mixed verify, padding, owner reorder

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests for boundary planning logic (causal, 256/512 isolation, virtual padding)
- [x] Full corpus regression (620 responses, token-exact)
- [x] NPU bit-exact matrix (160 cases)
- [ ] Upstream CI validation

This fix was developed and validated on vllm-ascend with CANN 8.5.1 on Ascend 910.

title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Prepare layerwise state before forward hooks
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Align AscendStore's layerwise state lifecycle with the deferred `start_load_kv()` contract introduced by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53333.

When a step has no synchronous KV loads, the runner binds metadata before the main-model forward but may call `start_load_kv()` only after that forward. AscendStore currently initializes its layer cursor, transfer task lists, prefetch cursor and attention gate in `start_load_kv()`. Consequently, the layer hooks can consume empty or stale state. With MTP, the deferred call can then reset the cursor and replace the tasks between the main-model and draft forwards.

Move per-step preparation to `bind_connector_metadata()`, following the upstream LMCache lifecycle. Keep actual layerwise load submission in `wait_for_layer_load()`. A deferred start must not discard the already prepared state or Mamba copy buffers. Preserve fresh task-list ownership across steps and leave the non-layerwise loading path unchanged.

This does not mutate `SchedulerOutput`, force synchronous loading, or skip the final/MTP layer. The allocation rounding issue is separate and remains in #16926; its code is not duplicated here.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes layerwise save/load state corruption when load submission is deferred, including steps that run MTP after the main forward. No new flags or configuration changes.

title: [WIP][Feature] Support encoder-side SWA Bounded Replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Ports upstream **Encoder-side SWA bounded replay** (vLLM [#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227)) to Ascend, for DeepSeek-V4.1 on model runner V1.

On a prefix hit upstream rewinds the request to `replay_start = H - min(window, H)`, recomputes the hit's last window, and keeps the sliding-window KV out of the prefix cache so that the recompute is what rebuilds it: the group gets `prefix_cacheable=False` and `prefix_replay_tokens=window`, and the scheduler only ever names a request that it rewound.  The positions below `replay_start` were retired and replaced by the null block, whose KV upstream documents as all-zero: a window reaching into them does not read another request's data, it reads phantom keys that score zero and take weight in the replayed token's softmax -- wrong, quiet, and only on a prefix hit. Upstream applies the clamp per request inside its SWA kernel (`start_pos = max(start_pos, replay_start)`); this PR is the Ascend equivalent, in five parts.

- **Read side** (`attention/dsa_v41.py`) -- `build_replay_swa_visible_lens` turns `replay_start` into a per-token visible ori KV length and hands it to `npu_sparse_flash_mla` through `ori_topk_length` in band mode. The operator bounds a window with one scalar for the whole call (`ori_win_left`), which cannot express a per-token floor, so the floor travels on the one channel that can. Every layer reads the ori side from the same `metadata.swa`, so no layer escapes the floor.
- **Write side** (`worker/block_table.py`, `ops/triton/compute_slot_mapping.py`) -- a Triton pass writes `PAD_SLOT_ID` over the replayed positions of every prefix-cacheable group, so the replayed recompute cannot land in blocks still shared with other requests that hit the same prefix. The bounded-replay sliding-window group is the one that keeps writing them, because that write is what rebuilds its window.
- **Carrier** (`worker/model_runner_v1.py`, `attention/utils.py`) -- a per-request `replay_start` buffer on the runner, rebuilt from zero every step on the CPU and carried to the backends on `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata`. It is `None` rather than zeros on a step that does not replay, so a dummy/profiling/capture batch cannot inherit the previous real step's values.
- **Scheduler** (`patch/platform/patch_swa_bounded_replay.py`) -- upstream reports a rewind on `NewRequestData` only, because its V2 runner folds resumed requests into the new-request list. The V1 runner resumes a preempted request through `CachedRequestData`, and a resumed request is exactly the one that can be rewound a second time (preemption clears the computed count, so readmission runs the lookup again), so the field is declared on that payload and filled from the resumed requests.
- **Operator** (`csrc/attention/sparse_flash_mla/`) -- band mode now reads `ori_topk_length` as a per-token visible length and floors the window's left edge at `right - count + 1`: arch22 in the SWA block-vector mask and in the CSA band setup, arch35 in `ComputeS2LoopInfo` before `oriKvLoopEndIdx` (on that path the loop count is the only mask there is). The width stays the scalar `ori_win_left`, so the band remains the upper bound and a supplied count can only narrow it.

`_downgrade_swa_bounded_replay` additionally turns the switch off at startup for the Ascend scheduling modes whose `schedule()` is a pinned copy of an older upstream body: they cannot rewind a prefix hit at all, so they must not have the switch on. `resolve_bounded_replay` keeps upstream's other two conditions and adds nothing of its own.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, for DeepSeek-V4.1 on model runner V1 only. Prefix hits now recompute the hit's last window instead of reusing its KV, and the sliding-window group leaves the prefix cache (no new user flag -- upstream's switch defaults to on). That is a trade the feature makes deliberately: the window is rebuilt so it can be bounded at `replay_start`. Other models never read the switch, and the release lane has neither the field nor the constructor argument.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, CPU only (no NPU required), 58 new cases in 5 files:

- `tests/ut/worker/test_replay_slot_padding.py` (19) -- the write side: which group is padded, the pointers and window that reach the kernel launch, and the per-request `replay_start` build.
- `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_cache.py` (6) -- the read side: the per-token counts for a replayed batch, for a step that does not replay, and for the requests in the same batch that are not replaying.
- `tests/ut/core/test_kv_cache_interface.py` (15) -- the spec gate, and the group merge carrying `bounded_replay` across.
- `tests/ut/core/test_swa_replay_downgrade.py` (9) -- the scheduling modes that must turn the switch off.
- `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_swa_bounded_replay.py` (9) -- the `CachedRequestData` field surviving msgpack and being filled from resumed requests.

**Not executed locally.** This branch was written on a machine without vLLM or an NPU, so the unit tests above and e2e tests have not been run.

**Not yet covered**

1. Operator equivalence for a single `npu_sparse_flash_mla` call: band mode with a count >= the window must be bit-identical to band mode without a count, and with a count below it, equal to band mode with `ori_win_left` narrowed by hand. This is the check that the `csrc` change does nothing when it should do nothing.
2. That the PAD pass really reaches the slot mappings the kernels read -- i.e. that a shared block's KV bytes are unchanged after a replay step.
3. DeepSeek-V4.1 e2e, gsm8k two-pass with the switch on vs off: first pass flat, second within 0.5pt, and a TTFT drop on the second pass.

title: [Feature][CI] Add persistent incremental csrc build cache
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

vLLM Ascend currently has an exact csrc artifact cache. It is very fast on an exact match, but any tracked csrc change invalidates the whole artifact and forces the native source build to start from scratch.

This PR adds a persistent, fine-grained L1 cache for csrc compilation while keeping the existing exact artifact cache as L0:

```text
L0 exact final artifact
        |
        | miss
        v
L1 persistent per-action cache
        |
        v
ordinary source build
```

L0 remains the only cache layer that can skip the whole native build. On an L0 miss, L1 restores a compatible set of candidate entries, then the normal source build runs. Each compiler action independently recomputes its identity and either reuses a verified entry or executes the original compiler command.

The source build therefore remains authoritative: an L1 miss, unavailable remote cache, or unsupported source snapshot falls back to the ordinary build.

### Cache identity and correctness

Each cached action is keyed by three semantic identities:

```text
prepared_input_hash
recipe_hash
compiler_environment_hash
```

The local cache engine in `csrc/scripts/build_cache.py` validates the action key, schema, artifact model, manifest, and artifact contents before accepting a HIT.

Prepared inputs cover generated operator sources, shared kernel sources, recipe files, and shared compatibility headers such as `cann_compat.h`. Explicit checkout/build roots may be normalized for UTF-8 text so equivalent workspaces can share entries, while binary content, external paths, symlink identity/targets, and semantic file contents remain sensitive.

The cache also preserves the build's concurrency and publication invariants:

- atomic local entry save;
- entry/action/publish locks with separate failure semantics;
- private staging for custom operators;
- artifact ownership tracking and collision detection;
- safe manifest/path validation before restored artifacts are used.

The persistent outer snapshot is only a transport/candidate-selection layer. It is not the correctness authority; inner action validation always decides whether an entry may be reused.

See the [design document](docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/persistent_csrc_build_cache.md) for the full contract.

### Persistent L1 transport

CI persists the local action cache through `runs-on/cache` using the existing Huawei OBS S3-compatible backend.

`prepare_csrc_l1_restore.py` is the shared key-preparation helper. It:

- detects whether the tested source contains the cache engine;
- derives the tracked-csrc identity;
- builds the compatibility/snapshot keys; and
- exports the local cache and telemetry paths.

Persistent callers use workflow-owned same-repository actions:

```text
$/.github/actions/csrc-l1-restore
$/.github/actions/csrc-l1-save
```

This intentionally separates workflow implementation from the source being tested. A caller may build a PR, fork, external repository, or historical ref without requiring that source snapshot to carry the current CI action implementation.

The restore action resets the `.updated` marker. The local engine creates that marker only when a new/replaced entry is successfully saved. Trusted writers therefore publish an updated shared snapshot only when the local L1 actually changed; an all-HIT build does not republish the same cache.

Historical source that predates `csrc/scripts/build_cache.py` is explicitly unsupported by L1:

```text
supported=false
→ skip L1 export/save
→ continue the original wheel/image/source build unchanged
```

No cache engine is injected or backported into old source snapshots.

### Trust and failure model

Shared L1 publication is limited to trusted producer paths, including the central csrc producer, image builds, and release wheel builds. PR-triggered nightly, selected tests, doctest/source consumers, and other consumer paths restore only.

The failure boundary is intentional:

```text
cache availability / performance failure
→ fail open to ordinary source compilation

integrity / correctness violation
→ fail safely
```

Examples of fail-open cases include remote MISS, unavailable OBS transport, missing writer credentials, unsupported historical source, or an unavailable optional snapshot.

Unsafe manifests, artifact ownership collisions, or synchronization failures that would make publication correctness ambiguous are not treated as cache misses.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No model-serving API or runtime behavior changes.

This PR only changes native csrc build/CI caching and related diagnostics.

### How was this patch tested?

The implementation was validated at three levels: the local cache engine, isolated CI workflow/component paths in the CI development repository, and formal vLLM Ascend CI.

#### 1. Cache engine and static correctness

- [CI-dev cache review validation — run 35215229554](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35215229554): cache-engine/concurrency tests, targeted mypy, production workflow YAML parsing, credential-less coordinator contract, and whitespace checks all passed.
- The cache suite covers content-addressed HIT/MISS behavior, cross-root reuse, semantic invalidation, schema/artifact validation, unsafe manifest/path rejection, symlink semantics, atomic save, and concurrency/ownership behavior.

The CI-dev repository is an isolated validation repository; access may be required. These runs validate production-equivalent snapshots/components and are not claimed to be final-head GitHub checks.

#### 2. Real source-build cold/warm reuse

Two real source-build environments were exercised through the persistent L1 workflow.

- `SOC_VERSION=ascend910_9391`
  - [cold run 34972671558](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/34972671558): 1 third-party + 248 custom-operator MISSes, followed by successful local saves.
  - [warm run 34974769880](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/34974769880): 1 third-party + 248 custom-operator HITs.
- `SOC_VERSION=ascend910b1`
  - [cold run 34972941408](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/34972941408): 1 third-party + 233 custom-operator MISSes, followed by successful local saves.
  - [warm run 34978189200](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/34978189200): 1 third-party + 233 custom-operator HITs.

These runs exercise real CMake/source compilation rather than synthetic cache-only actions.

#### 3. CI workflow/component integration

Representative successful CI-dev workflow validations:

- [central producer — run 35044413981](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35044413981): restore L1, install/build vllm-ascend, verify csrc artifacts, summarize the incremental cache, save L1, and save the exact csrc artifact.
- [A2 wheel path — run 35044420071](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35044420071): restore isolated wheel L1, build the wheel image, export the updated cache from the container, and save the snapshot.
- [A2 image path — run 35045094174](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35045094174): restore image-build L1, build a real Docker image, export the updated container cache, and save it.
- [doctest/source-install path — run 35084117212](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35084117212): prepare/restore L1, run the real source-install doctest path, collect cache telemetry, inspect the cache, and save the updated snapshot.

These component runs are intentionally listed here because they exercise the production workflow shapes independently, including the host/container cache-export boundary.

#### 4. TEST OBS transport, compatibility fallback, and concurrent reads

- [TEST OBS transport validation — run 35215229511](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35215229511):
  - a producer created a real cold action entry and published an L1 snapshot;
  - a same-csrc consumer restored the snapshot and obtained an inner HIT;
  - a compatible historical-csrc consumer restored through the compatibility fallback and obtained an inner HIT; and
  - an incompatible environment remained cold.
- [TEST OBS concurrent-read validation — run 35950570455](https://github.com/vllm-ascend-ci-dev/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35950570455), TEST-ONLY validation SHA `513c588750a33ca4fb2622a54f51ba712fb54cd9`: one producer saved a small L1 snapshot; 32 read-only consumers on 32 distinct `ubuntu-latest` runners restored its exact key. All 32 succeeded and verified the same three-file snapshot digest, with no key or content mismatch. The measured restore-and-verification windows reached 20 overlapping consumers; median elapsed time was 4.27 s and P95 was 6.48 s. The same run's separate same-csrc and compatibility consumers also verified inner HIT.

These TEST OBS runs validate small-snapshot transport reuse, compatibility fallback, and concurrent read behavior in the CI development repository. They do **not** establish production OBS credential access, large-snapshot throughput, sustained load, or production-runner concurrency.

#### 5. Formal vLLM Ascend CI

- [formal E2E run 35493648769](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35493648769) exercised `$/.github/actions/csrc-l1-restore` on the repository's Kubernetes-backed selected-test runner topology. The same-repository action resolved and executed successfully, the incremental restore step completed, and downstream vllm-ascend source installation remained healthy.

This is important because the workflow-owned `$/` action reference is the production path used to avoid coupling action resolution to the tested checkout/container workspace.

The final historical-source fail-open behavior is also guarded at workflow level: when key preparation reports `supported=false`, Docker wheel/image builds remain reachable while L1 export and save steps are skipped.
